scope: Refresh standalone ACIS peer admission against the latest published package contract and screen an MIT wrapper whose runtime depends on a separately licensed proprietary ACIS SDK.

method.kind: Read-only primary package/repository documentation and plan review
method.evidenceBoundary: The published CADMPEG 0.6.1 contract identifies verified ACIS 217/218 bands and an explicit unverified-dialect recovery route for other bands. Geometry transfer does not erase that loss. ACIS-Python3 is a wrapper requiring separately licensed Spatial SDK headers/libraries, not an open-source ACIS implementation. No runtime behavior, local defect, support promotion, or external-J resolution was established.

evidence.topic: CADMPEG published version admission and loss reporting
observed: docs.rs lists cadmpeg-codec-sat 0.6.1, released 2026-10-12, with caret dependencies on cadmpeg-asm, cadmpeg-core, and cadmpeg-ir ^0.6.1; an actual run therefore requires a resolved dependency lock and exact package/source identity.
The published reader describes Spatial ACIS 217/218 binary bands as verified.
Other ACIS bands can follow a nearest-verified-grammar decode path marked Admission::Unverified and report source.kernel-dialect-unverified.
The result separately reports geometry_transferred and losses; geometry_transferred does not clear an unverified dialect or establish complete/correct shape semantics.
The project identifies SAT/ACIS at L1 and documents unresolved topology, pcurve, body-kind inference, and procedural-normal cases.
doesNotEstablish: that any unverified recovered model is semantically correct
DWG/DXF container parsing, AcDs extraction, entity-to-payload ownership, or native CAD acceptance
an independent expected geometry oracle from the peer's own tests or same-codec stages
evidence.planUse: At the existing composed peer gate, classify Admission::Unverified, source.kernel-dialect-unverified, blocking geometry losses, and shape-relevant unknown records as diagnostic/non-promoting even if geometry is returned. For verified bands, require independently authored expected topology/metrics and complete per-body disposition.

evidence.topic: Open-source wrapper versus proprietary ACIS runtime
observed: The repository describes its code as a Python wrapper around Spatial's 3D ACIS Modeler, not as the ACIS SDK or an independently implemented SAT/SAB reader.
Building the wrapper requires separately obtained ACIS headers and libraries, and its README notes that a developer or university license may be required.
The README documents Python 3.5/3.6 support, so its runtime suitability is also an open qualification item.
doesNotEstablish: a freely available executable or SDK
current platform/version compatibility, or an available macOS ARM64 route
open-source peer status based solely on the wrapper's MIT license
evidence.planUse: Exclude from open-source parser/kernel counts. If an already lawfully available compatible SDK is used, record it as an optional licensed native-kernel witness with exact SDK/runtime and platform identity; do not acquire it or make it a local implementation prerequisite.

evidence.topic: OCCT open-source core and commercial ACIS translator boundary
observed: The current OCCT product documentation distinguishes the open-source modeling core from commercial data-exchange components, including ACIS translation.
An OCCT/FreeCAD kernel result is not evidence that stock open-source OCCT or FreeCAD has a general ACIS SAT/SAB importer.
doesNotEstablish: a commercial translator run on the local payload
kernel independence between FreeCAD and OCCT-based cq-acis routes
DWG AcDs association or native end-user acceptance
evidence.planUse: Keep parser independence, kernel lineage, licensed translator evidence, DWG/DXF wrapper correctness, and consumer acceptance as separate evidence axes.
